headline: Three days after the M7.7 Azuero earthquake, damage counts keep rising: SINAPROC now reports 1,293 homes damaged and ~619 schools affected, with about 570 people in shelters and no deaths.
key_points: Official (SINAPROC Communiqué 7, Sun noon): 0 deaths, 0 missing, 29 injured; 1,293 homes damaged; ~619 schools; ~570 people in shelters.
Village-level damage is severe: La Miel (95% of homes) and Bajo Corral (90%) in Las Tablas; 300+ homes collapsed in Los Pozos (mayor); ~1,500 affected in Mariato villages.
Tonosí: hospital unusable — care in tents; new US$30M hospital announced. Power and water still out in Tonosí, Mariato, Soná and Pedasí areas.
Schools: 419 affected, 24 need rebuilding; no classes nationwide on Monday 12 Oct.
Emergency decree (Res. 108, to 31 Dec): US$100M fast-track funds, may rise. IDB up to US$300M + US$500k; CAF US$50M; US$5M from US State Dept.
Aftershocks continue: 256 recorded (Instituto de Geociencias). Storm warning raises landslide risk; US$5M from the US confirmed by its embassy.

areas.text: Partial collapse of Hotel Dos Continentes; San Juan Bautista cathedral tower fell onto a car; Gobernación wall collapsed; market damaged (1 injured); Hospital Aquilino Tejeira cracked and evacuated; Iguana Mall damaged.
Cut off except via Macaracas; mayor's SOS: no power or water, food and medicine running short. Homes collapsed; 8 fracture patients airlifted; aid arriving by helicopter.

~1,500 affected in Llano Catival, Quebro, Arenas and El Cacao; Arenas, Quebro and El Cacao cut off; rural water systems collapsed; ~255 people in Mariato shelters. Montijo islands (Leones, Cébaco, Gobernadora) cut off, boats sunk; 55 homes damaged in Montijo town.

areas.area: Las Tablas rural villages, Los Santos
areas.text: La Miel: 95% of homes affected, many total losses, no aid yet; Bajo Corral: 90% affected, roads blocked by landslides; Bayano (La Canoa, Taboga): most homes a total loss.
El Sitio hostel collapsed. Locals told La Prensa people were trapped, but local authorities say the damaged tourist buildings in Pedasí were unoccupied. No official confirmation of anyone trapped.
Cathedral and municipal building damaged (partial roof collapse); bus terminal and Policlínica Horacio Díaz Gómez damaged.
Soná fire station damaged; road to Torio (Mariato) split with vertical offsets; Santiago–Arenas road cut. M6.6 aftershock at 20:25 UTC centred 14 km W of Río Grande (Soná).
Part of the Basílica Menor tower collapsed.

areas.area: Los Pozos, Las Minas, Pesé & Ocú, Herrera
areas.text: Hundreds of homes collapsed in Los Pozos (mayor); ~100 homes with considerable damage in Las Minas; over half of homes destroyed in Mandinga, Pesé (deputy); parish churches damaged; school ceiling collapse in Ocú.
Ceiling collapse in a school/university building (Telemundo video). Sunday Guardian, citing Telemetro, reports significant damage to at least six buildings — unconfirmed.
Broken windows on Calle 50 and Paitilla; hospitals evacuated as a precaution; Metro lines 1 and 2 suspended; Tocumen airport closed.
Considerable structural cracks at the Macaracas fire station (Fire Brigade via SINAPROC). Strong modelled shaking; few other reports so far.

Hospital del Oriente Chiricano (San Félix) fully evacuated, ~209 people (MINSA); damage at Puerto Armuelles hospital and Tolé health centre; cracked hotel facade and fire station in David; 15+ schools damaged. Shops and homes affected in the Pearl Islands; minor school damage in Darién.

services.text: Naturgy has restored 97% of affected customers; Mariato, Soná, Atalaya, Tonosí, Flores and Pedasí still pending.

Treatment plants damaged nationwide; Chilibre (most of Panama City and San Miguelito) back to 70% after falling to 20%. CSS suspended hemodialysis nationwide due to water shortage; Monte Esperanza (Colón) tanks damaged but pumping.
Widespread mobile and internet failures across several operators.
Tocumen International closed and evacuated; flights diverted to Barranquilla, Cartagena, Bogotá, San José, Managua and Panamá Pacífico.
Road to Torio (Mariato) ruptured; Santiago–Arenas road cut; damage around Cambutal.
Operating normally; ACP denied rumours of damage to Agua Clara locks.
419 schools affected, 24 need rebuilding; no classes nationwide on Monday 12 Oct (MEDUCA).
PTWC initially warned of 1–3 m waves on Panama's coasts; later no Pacific-wide threat. No tsunami damage reported.
Panama City municipality suspended all municipal services, including markets, until further notice.

upcoming: Counts expected to keep rising as unreachable communities are assessed; MIVIOT housing census and next SINAPROC communiqué expected.
unknowns: Homes destroyed (only Chiriquí's 10 reported) and the final housing count — MIVIOT housing census under way.
When access, power and water will be restored to Tonosí and the Mariato coast.
Whether heavy rain triggers further landslides on damaged slopes and roads.
When schools will reopen and how many need structural repair.
Full cost of damage — no official estimate yet.
